description: Project-defined undergraduate foundation scope, not a universal curriculum standard. Each mode describes a broad problem form, not every exercise subtype. Credits require explicit source bindings; no automatic topic inference.

problem_forms.recognize: Identify and state the assumptions for solvability and uniqueness.
problem_forms.compute_construct: Compute or construct solutions of a linear system.
problem_forms.justify_prove: Prove under explicit assumptions a consistency or solution-space criterion.
problem_forms.counterexample_audit: Construct or explain a counterexample to inconsistent or nonunique systems.
problem_forms.synthesize: Combine results involving solution sets and kernel/image.

problem_forms.recognize: Identify and state the assumptions for matrix dimensions and operation laws.
problem_forms.compute_construct: Compute or construct matrix products, inverses, or powers.
problem_forms.justify_prove: Prove under explicit assumptions a matrix operation identity.
problem_forms.counterexample_audit: Construct or explain a counterexample to invalid matrix operation laws.
problem_forms.synthesize: Combine results involving several matrix operations.

problem_forms.recognize: Identify and state the assumptions for subspace conditions.
problem_forms.compute_construct: Compute or construct a subspace sum or intersection.
problem_forms.justify_prove: Prove under explicit assumptions closure or an inclusion between subspaces.
problem_forms.counterexample_audit: Construct or explain a counterexample to a set failing a subspace condition.
problem_forms.synthesize: Combine results involving subspaces and linear maps.

problem_forms.synthesize: Combine results involving spanning, independence, and linear maps.
